title: Loadbench field notebook — concurrency mosaic
content:
Lab notebook: loadbench field investigations — concurrency mosaic

Author: Marta Lopez (primary), notes & raw observations. Intended as an operational notebook for teams running long-form throughput sweeps across heterogeneous GPU profiles. Not a polished playbook — living doc, raw logs and heuristics.

Objective:
- Understand why throughput at medium concurrency (8–32 sessions) shows large run-to-run variance on A100 vs RTX8000 nodes.
- Produce a repeatable harness recipe (configs + checklist) that reduces run variance to <3% p95 across 3 independent runs.
- Capture warmup/priming heuristics that reliably saturate KV-cache and allocator behavior without thermal-induced throttling.

Background & hypothesis summary (quick):
- Observed: throughput drops mid-run on some nodes after ~12–18 minutes; tail latency spikes and token/sec dips correlate with GPU frequency/thermal telemetry.
- Hypothesis 1: long-running allocator churn (CUDA memory fragmentation) interacts with batching causing GC-like latency spikes.
- Hypothesis 2: KV-cache coldness + variable sequence-length mix leads to kernel selection jitter; runtime switches slower quantized kernels mid-run.
- Hypothesis 3: ambient thermal drift causes power capping, combined with execution hotspot that magnifies throughput variance.

Hardware / infra inspected:
- A100 40GB (pod-a100-1a), RTX8000 48GB (pod-rtx-1b), V100 legacy (pod-v100-3c) — batch sizes varied per device.
- Driver/nvidia stack: 525.xx on A100 nodes, 535.xx on RTX nodes (note differences).
- Borg/Orchestration: isolated bench pools with no colocated tenants for these runs.

Experiment setup (high level):
- Load generator: benchgen v0.9.2 (internal) with sessioned clients; supports sequence length sampling, prefix caching control, and deterministic RNG seeds.
- Measurement window: 900s warmup + 1800s steady collection (unless noted).
- Observables: aggregate tokens/sec, per-client qps, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU util, gpu_power_draw, sm_efficiency, temp_gpu, nvlink traffic, OS-level interrupts, allocator churn counters.

Canonical loadgen config (text snippet to copy):
--- benchgen config snippet ---
clients: 128
sessions_per_client: 8
sequence_length_distribution: |
  - 40: 0.45
  - 128: 0.35
  - 512: 0.20
sampling_seed: 4321
kv_cache_mode: "prefix-only"  # options: none, prefix-only, full-body
batching_policy: "latency-aware"
max_batch_tokens: 2048
target_concurrency: 24
arrival_pattern: "poisson"
warmup_policy: "staircase-primed"
--- end snippet ---

Key differences from prior runs: explicit sampling_seed for repeatability, kv_cache_mode toggles, and warmup_policy set to staircase-primed (see heuristics below).

Warmup & priming heuristics (practical recipe):
1) Pre-warm KV cache: send 3x the expected prefix combinations across a small fleet of priming clients (low qps, high coverage) for 120s. This warms token-level KV and reduces first-write allocator churn.
2) Staircase prime: start at 1% target concurrency for 30s, 5% for 45s, 20% for 60s, 50% for 90s, then hold at target_concurrency for 300s before entering collection window.
3) Allocator stabilizer: after steady concurrency hold for 300s, run a lightweight GC-probe (allocate/dealloc dummy tensors) to exercise allocator paths without generating model work — 3 cycles of 10s on/10s off.
4) Thermal ramp guard: ensure node GPU temp < 60C before start; if >60C, idle for 180s and recheck. Tag run as "warm" if starting >60C.

Repeatability checklist (must pass before marking run valid):
- [ ] benchgen sampling_seed set and logged (seed: 4321)
- [ ] No concurrent jobs on the same node (check orchestration tags)
- [ ] Driver/kernel versions recorded
- [ ] Node thermal baseline < 60C prior to run
- [ ] KV-cache priming completed (priming client logs present)
- [ ] Sequence-length histogram captured and matches intended distribution within ±2% per bucket
- [ ] Hardware telemetry capture enabled and healthy (NVML metrics streaming)
- [ ] Run label including experiment-id + seed + node-id applied to all artifacts

Profiling checklist (for when variance persists):
- Collect nsight-systems for 60s slices immediately before and after any observed throughput dip.
- Dump runtime allocator counters at 10s cadence: total_alloc_calls, total_free_calls, peak_allocated_bytes, fragmentation_ratio.
- Capture kernel selection logs (runtime -> kernel/primitive choices) for 2-minute intervals.
- Collect pprof stacks from inference workers to capture Python/host-side stalls (locks, I/O).

Run-notes (selected raw entries):
2025-01-10 09:30 (pod-a100-1a, seed=4321)
- Started priming clients at 09:30:12, 120s coverage completed 09:32:12; verified ~98% prefix coverage for our canonical prompt set.
- Staircase: 1%->5%->20%->50% took 255s total; held at target=24 concurrency for 300s.
- Collection window (1800s) initial 10m tokens/sec stable within 1.8%. At t=15m observed 9% dip in tokens/sec concurrent with GPU clock drop from 1365->1120 MHz. GPU temp rose from 63->72C over 8m.
- NSYS snippet (captured 60s) shows increased PCIe serialization and several host-to-device memcpy stalls coincident with kernel queue backlog.
- Allocator counters: spike in new allocations at t=14m with fragmentation_ratio up to 0.31 (baseline 0.08).
- Conclusion: likely thermal throttling combined with fragmentation-triggered kernel path changes.

2025-01-12 14:00 (pod-rtx-1b, seed=4321)
- Same config ran on RTX8000. No immediate thermal ramp (start 48C). Throughput variance high but no clock drop. Host-side pprof shows occasional thread contention around batch packing thread; switching to increased packer threads from 4->8 reduced p95 by ~9%.
- KV-cache mode full-body vs prefix-only: full-body reduced per-token compute by ~2% but increased memory churn; on RTX this pushed fragmentation up, causing minor throughput dips after ~30m.

Mitigations tested and notes:
- Throttle steady-state: add 30s micro-idle (sleep 0.2s every 60s) — reduces thermal drift and stabilizes clocks, but yields net -1.5% throughput. Worthwhile when reproducibility > raw throughput.
- Pre-allocation slab strategy: reserve 90% of peak working set at startup; eliminated allocator spikes on A100 runs but increased initial start latency and required memory headroom. Best for Dedicated runs where we can guarantee memory.
- Batch-packer parallelism tuning: bumping packer threads helped RTX nodes; no change on A100 where kernel launch dominates.

Observability & log conventions to adopt (operational):
- Annotate run metadata with: experiment-id, benchgen-seed, node-id, driver-version, firmware, run-operator, kv-cache-mode, warmup-policy, warm-label.
- Create a short hash of sequence-length histogram and store in artifact metadata for quick diffs.
- Persist allocator counters to a time-series metric with 10s resolution for correlation plots.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Does driver version 535.xx on A100 avoid fragmentation spike? Schedule A/B test with 525 vs 535.
- Can runtime adopt a background compaction pass triggered when fragmentation_ratio > 0.2 that avoids stalling token generators? Prototype idea: offload compaction to a low-priority worker.
- Evaluate effect of different KV-cache priming patterns: dense coverage vs targeted hot-prefix only. Does denser priming reduce total alloc churn?
- Quantized kernel path hysteresis: why does runtime sometimes switch to slower fallback kernel mid-run? Need deeper kernel selection trace.

Immediate action items (who/when):
- Ethan: schedule 3x A/B runs between 525 and 535 drivers on A100 nodes (due 2025-01-20).
- Priya: instrument allocator counters into TSDB with 10s scrape (due 2025-01-17).
- Marta: prototype pre-allocation hook in bench runtime; basic toggle to reserve memory slabs (due 2025-01-22).

Appendix: quick reproducibility command examples
- Launch bench run (example):
  benchgen run --config configs/concurrency-mosaic.yaml --seed 4321 --label "exp/concurrency-mosaic/a100-1a-20250110" --telemetry nsys,tsdb,alloc_counters

- Quick check script (pseudo):
  ./check_run.sh --label exp/concurrency-mosaic/a100-1a-20250110
  # verifies seed, node-id, seq-histogram, kv-prime logs, telemetry presence

Closing note: this notebook is intentionally pragmatic and fragmentary. The goal is to converge on a small, repeatable harness that trades a bit of sustained throughput for reproducibility and observability. Most variance we've seen so far is multi-factor (thermal + allocator + packing). Next focus: isolate thermal vs alloc with constrained-memory pre-alloc runs and driver A/B test.

End of entry.
